blocks.text: This video shows how to put an animation from Pixodesk 2D Animator into a React app, as a Lottie file. It takes one package, one file and one component. Let's start with the app as it is.

blocks.alt: A heading, and nothing that moves yet.

blocks.text: A heading, and nothing that moves yet. To play Lottie files, the app needs a Lottie player. Let's install lottie react.

blocks.alt: Lottie react is in, one package.

blocks.text: Lottie react is in, one package. Now for the animation itself. Let's switch to the editor, where a football is already drawn.

blocks.alt: It's a vector drawing, standing still.

blocks.text: It's a vector drawing, standing still. To make it move, let's switch on Auto mode.

blocks.alt: With Auto mode on, every change becomes a keyframe.

blocks.text: With Auto mode on, every change becomes a keyframe. Half a second in, let's drag the ball down to the floor.

blocks.alt: A keyframe appears on the timeline, holding the new position.

blocks.text: A keyframe appears on the timeline, holding the new position. At one second, let's bring it back up.

blocks.alt: Now it falls and rises again, in one second.

blocks.text: Now it falls and rises again, in one second. A real ball speeds up as it falls, and slows down as it rises. Let's set that easing.

blocks.alt: Gravity easing, falling and rising, makes the bounce feel natural.

blocks.text: Gravity easing, falling and rising, makes the bounce feel natural. The animation is ready. Let's save it as Lottie JSON, straight into the project.

blocks.alt: The animation file is already there, next to the code.

blocks.text: The animation file is already there, next to the code. Let's import the Lottie component, and the animation file.

blocks.alt: The component comes from lottie react, the animation from the JSON file.

blocks.text: The component comes from lottie react, the animation from the JSON file. Then, let's place it on the page.

blocks.alt: Its source is the animation. Autoplay starts it when the page loads, and loop repeats it.

blocks.text: Its source is the animation. Autoplay starts it when the page loads, and loop repeats it. Let's reload the page, and watch.

blocks.alt: There it is. The ball bounces, right inside the React app.

blocks.text: There it is. The ball bounces, right inside the React app. So, one package, one Lottie file saved from the editor, and one component. That's all it takes to bring an animation into a React app.
